en: To Him whose half-body is the golden hue of a Champaka flower, and whose other half-body is the white hue of camphor.
Salutation to Dhammillakā and Jaṭādharā; salutation to Śivā and to Śiva. ||1||
Salutations to Śivā, who is anointed with musk and saffron, yet covered in heaps of funeral ashes; salutations to Śiva, who has aroused passion, yet whose passion is extinguished. ||2||

Salutations to Śivā, whose lotus-feet possess moving, jingling bracelets and anklets, and whose silver anklets are like serpents; salutations to Śiva, who wears golden armlets and whose limbs are adorned with serpents. 3.

Salutations to her whose eyes are like broad blue lotuses, salutations to her whose eyes are like blooming lotuses; salutations to the one with even eyes and salutations to the one with uneven eyes; salutations to Śivā and salutations to Śiva. ||4||

Salutations to her whose locks are adorned with mandāra garlands, and to him whose neck is marked by a garland of skulls; salutations to her clad in divine raiment, and to him who is naked; salutations to Śivā and salutations to Śiva. 5.

Salutations to Śivā, who possesses locks of hair as dark as rain-clouds; salutations to Śiva, who bears matted locks tawny with the luster of lightning; salutations to the one who is without a lord; salutations to the Lord of all. 6.

Salutations to Śivā and salutations to Śiva—the one whose body performs the dance intent on creating the manifold world, who performs the *tāṇḍava* of universal dissolution, who is the mother of the universe, and who is the sole father of the universe. (7)
Salutations to her who possesses earrings blazing with radiant jewels and who is adorned with shimmering great serpents;
salutations to her who is accompanied by Śiva, and salutations to Śiva who is accompanied by her; salutations to Śivā and salutations to Śiva. (8)
Whoever recites these eight [verses] with devotion, which grant all desires, shall be honored on earth and live a long life;
he shall obtain good fortune for an infinite time, and may every accomplishment always belong to him. (9)

Thus ends the *Ardhanārīnaṭeśvara-stotra*, composed by the venerable Śaṅkara Bhagavat, disciple of the venerable Govinda Bhagavat-pūjyapāda, the illustrious wandering ascetic teacher (*paramahaṃsa-parivrājaka-ācārya*).
